records.text:
- Histopathologic Examination:  - Revealed perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates around cystically dilated follicular infundibula  - Exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes into the epithelium  - Admixed plasma cells, eosinophils, and multinucleate giant cells  - Alcian blue staining showed focal mild follicular mucin deposition
- Immunohistochemical Analysis:  - Lymphocytic infiltrates positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD7  - Negative for CD8, CD20, CD30, CD79a, and CD56  - CD4 to CD8 cells ratio within hair follicles > 7:1  - Monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement was demonstrated
- Images:  Image A Title: Clinical presentation of right upper eyelid  Image A Description: 4 × 2-cm erythematous, violaceous, indurated, scaly plaque with papules

records.text:
- Histopathologic Examination:  
  - Revealed perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates around cystically dilated follicular infundibula  
  - Exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes into the epithelium  
  - Admixed plasma cells, eosinophils, and multinucleate giant cells  
  - Alcian blue staining showed focal mild follicular mucin deposition  
- Immunohistochemical Analysis:  
  - Lymphocytic infiltrates positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD7  
  - Negative for CD8, CD20, CD30, CD79a, and CD56  
  - CD4 to CD8 cells ratio within hair follicles > 7:1  
  - Monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement was demonstrated

bindings.label: A man in his 60s presented with a pruritic, dark red plaque on his right upper eyelid for 1 year
Physical examination revealed a 4 × 2-cm erythematous, violaceous, indurated, scaly plaque with some papules on the right upper eyelid
The patient is a man in his 60s with no remarkable medical history
Histopathology report shows atypical lymphocytic exocytosis in the eyelid biopsy
Immunohistochemistry shows CD4-predominant infiltrate with CD4:CD8 ratio >7:1
T-cell gene rearrangement study detects a monoclonal T-cell population
Pathologist diagnoses mycosis fungoides involving the eyelid, a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
Mycosis fungoides (cutaneous T-cell lymphoma) involving the right upper eyelid
Laboratory physician analysis confirms mycosis fungoides involving the right upper eyelid and recommends completing staging workup
Staging workup for mycosis fungoides has not been performed (no flow cytometry, peripheral blood Sézary cell examination, or staging imaging)
Mycosis fungoides may have extracutaneous/systemic involvement
Mycosis fungoides (cutaneous T-cell lymphoma) involving the right upper eyelid
Pathologist analysis notes that no staging data were obtained despite multiple searches and recommends completing staging workup
Laboratory physician analysis states that extracutaneous involvement cannot be fully excluded because staging workup (flow cytometry, peripheral blood Sézary cell count, CT/PET) remains unavailable
No direct evidence of extracutaneous involvement or Sézary cells is currently available
Mycosis fungoides is currently confined to the skin (no extracutaneous involvement)
